summary: Sandusky Bay light on Lake Erie, built 1821 and first lit 1822; first keeper Benajah Wolcott, then his widow Rachel; automated 1958; now an Ohio state park.

light.note: USLHS: 67.5 ft above mean high water; current optic listed as a plastic beacon. The 2018 LED is visible for eleven nautical miles (Ohio marker).

structures.note: Built 1821 of local limestone; top 8 ft removed and brick extension added 1897; about 65 ft (19.8 m) after the changes (LighthouseFriends); USLHS gives 60 ft (18.3 m) from base to lantern center
Victorian keeper's dwelling, wood frame (USLHS); now a museum in season
Circular metal oil house, 1891 (LighthouseFriends); neither oil house stands today (LighthouseFriends)
White barn on the lighthouse property (USLHS)

access.note: Marblehead Lighthouse State Park (Ohio DNR). Tours daily noon to 4 p.m. from Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day, per LighthouseFriends; the dwelling museum is run by the Marblehead Lighthouse Historical Society.

events.note: Tower of limestone built from September to November (LighthouseFriends); USLHS year established 1821
Thirteen oil lamps lit by keeper Benajah Wolcott (Ohio marker)
Benajah Wolcott appointed 24 June 1822
Fourth-order Fresnel lens replaces reflectors
Lighthouse Board recommends $20,000 for rebuilding the station (LighthouseFriends)
Keeper's dwelling built
Circular oil house erected
Top eight feet removed; brick extension added to the tower
Marker timeline: a masonry watch room replaced and widened the tower's upper eight feet of stone (LighthouseFriends dates the top removal to 1897)
Lantern from the discontinued Erie Land Lighthouse placed on top (LighthouseFriends dates it 1900; Ohio marker dates it 1901)
Three-and-a-half-order Fresnel lens, 66 inches across each face, clockwork-driven
Assistant keeper position added to the station
Square iron oil house
Incandescent oil-vapor lamp installed
Electric light replaces kerosene
Coast Guard takes responsibility after the last civilian keeper retires
Light automated; tower restuccoed
On the National Register since 1969 (Ohio marker)
Fresnel lens removed; 300 mm plastic beacon installed (the Ohio marker dates the optic change to 1972)
Renovation removed the exterior stucco, showing the original stone and brickwork
Lens shipped to Detroit and returned to the town hall for display
Coast Guard declares the tower and plot surplus federal property (January 1997)
Ohio Department of Natural Resources takes ownership
Restoration of brickwork, tower and keeper's dwelling begins 1 September 2001 ($500,000)
Historic lens returned to display in the keeper's dwelling

corrections.why: The tower was completed in 1821; the Ohio markers say the lamps were first lit by Wolcott in 1822, after his appointment on 24 June 1822.
USLHS gives 1821 as the year the tower was established, and LighthouseFriends dates construction to September to November 1821.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: USLHS and LighthouseFriends date the tower to 1821. The Ohio marker dates the first lighting to 1822 under Wolcott. Both are kept: built 1821, first lit 1822.

Not resolved. Fifty feet (LighthouseFriends; marker 2 says 50 feet high) or 55 feet when built (lamps-and-lenses marker 1). After the 1897-1901 work: LighthouseFriends about 65 ft (19.8 m); marker 2 says the 1897-1900 addition raised the height 15 ft; marker 1's timeline gives 73 ft 6 in total after 1901; USLHS gives 60 ft (18.3 m) base to lantern center and 67.5 ft above mean high water. The story gives each figure with its source.

Not resolved. LighthouseFriends dates the Erie Land lantern to 1900 and the top removal to 1897; marker 1 dates the watch room to 1898 and the lantern to 1901 (third superstructure). The story gives both.
LighthouseFriends puts the removal of the Fresnel lens and the plastic 300 mm beacon in 1969; the Ohio marker puts the plastic optic in 1972. Not resolved.
One Ohio marker credits William Kelly with eight weeks; another credits John Kelly and his son and helpers with eleven weeks; LighthouseFriends says William Kelly and a crew of two men. Not resolved.

The Keeper's House marker (4) gives her service until February 1854. The USLHS roster (8) ends her post in 1834, when Van Benschoten is listed as keeper. The local history (5) says she had official charge for about two years, that the couple tended the light together for about eight years, and that she drops out of the lighthouse records at that point. The story reports all three; the 1854 date is not accepted.
One marker says he and a son died of cholera; the local history and LighthouseFriends mention only Benajah. Not resolved; the son is mentioned as the marker's claim only.
The record's 10.4 nm is older; the Ohio marker says the current LED is visible up to eleven nautical miles. The record's figure is not confirmed by a current source.
Record's 20.4 m is close to the USLHS 67.5 ft above mean high water (20.6 m). Taken from USLHS.

Marker 2 credits William Kelly with eight weeks; marker 1 credits John Kelly, his son and three helpers with eleven weeks; LighthouseFriends names William Kelly and two men. Marker 2 gives 50 ft high; marker 1 gives 55 ft when built.

notes_for_editor: Fact-check 2026-10-22 (Haiku). Roster matched by roster.py (name and position, 0.10 km) and checked against the cached USLHS page; the person slugs match. Consuelo (1876 Life-Saving report): the Awards text is at printed p. 28 (the report's index also gives 28), scan p. 33 (corpus.py page); the printed page was read from the index, not the image. The OCR garbles the brothers' names ('Lucien M demons'); the story names Lucien Clemons on LighthouseFriends' authority (cited [3]); later Life-Saving reports list Lucien M. Clemons as a medal recipient for this rescue. Consuelo narrative quotes are OCR text, checked by check_quotes; 'twelve feet long, three feet wide' and 'tremendous' should be spot-checked on scan p. 33 before any print use. Ferris (1880): the 15 October entry is at scan p. 78 (printed p. 71 unconfirmed, so no printed page is given); the station-list entry 'Station No. 9 (Marblehead Point, Ohio)' is at scan p. 64 (printed p. 57 unconfirmed). NRHP nomination (NRIS 69000148) is not digitised. Ohio DNR and Marblehead Lighthouse Historical Society pages returned 404 or 403 to fetch_text, so current hours come from LighthouseFriends and may be out of date. The 1877 and 1891 Lighthouse Board reports are not in the corpus for those years; the 1877 recommendation and the 1891 oil house come from LighthouseFriends only. The marker dates and LighthouseFriends dates conflict on the lantern (1900 vs 1901), the watch room (1897 vs 1898), the lens removal (1969 vs 1972) and the builder; each is stated in the story. Frank Skorupa appears only in the USLHS roster under the Coast Guard heading ('at least 1952-'); no other source was read, so no role beyond that is claimed. The Keeper's House marker (4) and the local history (5) disagree on Rachel Wolcott's service (see resolved_conflicts). The 1972 optic date and the 1900/1901 lantern dates remain conflicts. Wolcott's house (hmdb 87283) is off the light's grounds; it is described in the story but not listed as a station structure.
